Prioritise duration over pace; drink enough.
Only increase one load variable at a time (duration, distance or intensity). Increase volume only gradually; don't use a rigid 10% rule as a guarantee.
Recovery week in week 4; reduce earlier if you have pain or unusual fatigue.

At least 48 hours between hard running sessions.
Stop and get the cause checked if you have sharp, increasing pain or pain that changes your running style.
Three easy sessions, one of them a bit longer.
20–30 min easy + 4 × 15–20 s fast/relaxed with 60–90 s walking break
Four runs, mostly easy; only short strides as a technique stimulus.
Only do it if your legs and general condition feel good.
High frequency at mostly low intensity; adjust volume to your previous training.
All runs at a calm conversational intensity, no tempo session.
One intense and one easy session; not on consecutive days.

One interval session per week plus easy runs.

6 × (1 min brisk + 2 min easy), choose any terrain
Go by feel; keep the fast sections under control.
Easy pace changes without rigid pace targets.
One fartlek per week, supplemented by easy endurance runs.
Four sessions with one varied tempo day.
Use natural terrain instead of exact interval times.
35 min rolling terrain: climbs brisk, flat sections easy, downhill controlled
Go by perceived effort rather than pace.
Short fast sections with generous recovery.
The fast sections stay relaxed and technically clean.
One hill session and one easy run; plan enough recovery.
6 × 30–45 s powerfully uphill, walk easily back down
Short, moderate incline; don't sprint downhill.
Short hill intervals once a week.

50–70 min on varied terrain, walking sections on steep climbs allowed

Short hill efforts plus strides and a long run.

5 × 3 min at your target 5 km effort (RPE 8), 2 min jogging break
Choose a realistic target pace; even repetitions.
Five sessions with two quality sessions; only with enough running history.
